title: Representability facts for an affine etale-relation quotient
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U$ be an affine scheme over $S$, and let $(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be an etale equivalence relation with $s,t$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $F$ be the sheafification on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $T\mapsto U(T)/R(T)$. For every scheme $T$ over $S$ and map $T\to F$, the fibre product $T\times_F h_U$ is representable by a scheme over $T$; moreover, the diagonal map $F\to F\times F$ is representable (its pullback by every map from a scheme is a scheme).

source.place: Tag 0265 (presentation-quasi-compact), first and third representability steps; the proof uses Tags 02WU, 02WT, 023Q and the separated locally quasi-finite fppf descent lemmas.

proof.text: Put $j=(s,t)$ and $q:h_U\to F$. Here $h_Z(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(W,Z)$ for every $S$-scheme $Z$. Apply [lem-trf-affine-etale-relation-separated-lqf] to obtain that $s,t$ and $j$ are separated and locally quasi-finite. The hypotheses are precisely that $U$ is affine and $(s,t)$ is an etale equivalence relation; $S$ need not be separated.

Fix a scheme $T$ over $S$ and a map $a:h_T\to F$. Write $Q(W)=U(W)/R(W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], the section $a_T(\mathrm{id}_T)\in Q^\#(T)$ has representatives in $Q(T_i)$ on an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$. Choose representatives $a_i:T_i\to U$ of these equivalence classes. Naturality gives $a_W(g)=F(g)(a_T(\mathrm{id}_T))$ for every $g:W\to T$, so $q a_i=a|_{T_i}$ as natural transformations. This uses only the existence of local representatives, not representability or etaleness of $q$.

source.place: Tag 0265, first representability step, choice of an fppf cover and maps a_i.

proof.text: Let $G=h_T\times_F h_U$. The kernel-pair identity [lem-trf-etale-relation-kernel-pair] identifies its pullback to $T_i$ with $h_{X_i}$, where $X_i=T_i\times_{a_i,U,s}R$ and the map $X_i\to U$ is $t$ on the second factor. Explicitly, on a test scheme $W\to T_i$, a point of $G$ is a map $u:W\to U$ with $q(u)=q(a_i|_W)$; the kernel-pair identity gives a unique $r:W\to R$ with $s(r)=a_i|_W$ and $t(r)=u$. This is a natural bijection, so it gives the asserted representation. The structure map $X_i\to T_i$ is a base change of $s$ and is separated and locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change] and step 1.

source.place: Tag 0265, first representability step, displayed fibre-product calculation (with the two relation projections interchanged).

proof.text: Regard $G$ on the big fppf site of $T$ by $G(W)=\{u:W\to U\mid q(u)=a|_W\}$. The kernel-pair statement [lem-trf-etale-relation-kernel-pair] is an identity of fppf sheaves, so in particular $h_U$ is an fppf sheaf. Hence $G$ is a sheaf: the maps to $U$ glue uniquely on a cover, and their required equality in $F$ can be checked on that cover. Apply [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-representability-descent-data] to the local schemes $X_i$. Its overlap comparison maps give a scheme descent datum with these very $X_i$. They are separated and locally quasi-finite over $T_i$ by step 3, so [lem-trf-separated-lqf-fppf-effective-descent] makes this datum effective. The representability-if-effective clause of the former lemma then represents $G$ by a scheme over $T$. This proves the first assertion.

source.place: Tag 0265, end of the first representability step; Tags 02W5 and 02W8.

proof.text: Now fix $a:h_T\to F\times F$, with components $a_1,a_2$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] separately to these two quotient sections. Use pullback stability and composition of coverings, which are the site axioms in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], to take a common fppf refinement $\{T_i\to T\}$. There are maps $u_i,v_i:T_i\to U$ with $q(u_i)=a_1|_{T_i}$ and $q(v_i)=a_2|_{T_i}$. Hence $(u_i,v_i)$ is a map to $U\times_SU$.

source.place: Tag 0265, third representability step, local lift to U times U; taking fppf lifts directly replaces the unnecessary intervening verification that q is etale.

proof.text: Set $H=h_T\times_{F\times F,\Delta}F$. On $W\to T$, its sections are pairs consisting of the structure map and a section $z\in F(W)$ with $z=a_1|_W=a_2|_W$. Thus the fibre is a singleton exactly when $a_1|_W=a_2|_W$, and otherwise empty. On $T_i$ this sheaf is represented by $Y_i=T_i\times_{(u_i,v_i),U\times_SU,j}R$: the kernel-pair identity [lem-trf-etale-relation-kernel-pair] says that $q(u_i|_W)=q(v_i|_W)$ holds exactly when there is a unique $r:W\to R$ with $(s(r),t(r))=(u_i|_W,v_i|_W)$. This describes inverse natural maps on sections. The structure map $Y_i\to T_i$ is a base change of $j$, so it is separated and locally quasi-finite by step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0265, third representability step, cartesian square of j and Delta and its base change to T.

proof.text: The functor $H$ on the big fppf site of $T$ is a sheaf: equality of the two fixed sections of $F$ is local, with a unique section whenever they agree. By [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-representability-descent-data] the representing schemes $Y_i$ of step 6 carry the corresponding descent datum. By [lem-trf-separated-lqf-fppf-effective-descent] it is effective, since every $Y_i\to T_i$ is separated and locally quasi-finite. The representability-if-effective clause of the former lemma represents $H$ by a scheme over $T$. As $a$ was arbitrary, the diagonal of $F$ is representable.

source.place: Tag 0265, final paragraph, applications of Tags 02W5 and 02W8.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first and third representability steps; for the diagonal use the common fppf refinement of local representatives directly.

lean.statement: theorem etale_affine_quotient_representable {S : Scheme.{u}} {R U : Over S} [IsAffine U.left] (s t : R ⟶ U) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ U ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [Etale s.left] [Etale t.left] (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ F.obj) (hη : ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun g : F.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ g)) : IsRepresentable (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η) ∧ IsRepresentable (prod.lift (𝟙 F.obj) (𝟙 F.obj))
